title: Spatial Navigation Memory of Object Locations
description: This dataset contains intracranial electrophysiological recordings and behavioral data from a spatial navigation memory task conducted across multiple clinical sites. Participants encoded object locations during guided navigation learning phases and recalled them during self-navigation test phases. The study investigates memory mechanisms underlying spatial navigation through direct brain recordings in clinical populations.
methods_description: Intracranial EEG recordings were collected during a spatial navigation memory task consisting of 50 trials per session (2 practice, 48 experimental). Each trial included 2 learning phases with guided navigation to object locations and 1 test phase requiring self-navigation recall. Learning trials involved automatic navigation to objects over 3 seconds with 1-second orientation and pause periods. Test trials required participants to navigate to remembered object locations in a 64.8 x 36 unit virtual environment. Recordings were acquired using Blackrock (250 nV units) and Medtronic (0.1 µV units) systems with monopolar and bipolar electrode configurations.
